article.title: Giving constructive feedback professionally
article.description: Useful framework: start positive, then the specific issue, then a suggestion. Phrases: 'One thing that worked really well was...', 'One area to consider improving is...', 'Going forward, it might help to...'. Avoid absolute negative language like 'this is wrong' — softer framing keeps the conversation constructive.
article.content: Useful framework: start positive, then the specific issue, then a suggestion. Phrases: 'One thing that worked really well was...', 'One area to consider improving is...', 'Going forward, it might help to...'. Avoid absolute negative language like 'this is wrong' — softer framing keeps the conversation constructive.

generated.caption:
Want to give feedback that truly helps? 🤝
Always start with a positive, then gently address the issue, and finish with a helpful suggestion. This framework keeps your feedback constructive, not critical!

For example: "One thing that worked well was... One area to consider improving is... Going forward, it might help to..."

generated.script: Feedback dete time awkward ho jaate ho na, ki samne waala bura maan jaayega? Toh dekho, professional feedback dene ka ek simple framework hai. Pehle, hamesha start positive. Bolo, 'One thing that worked really well was...' Phir, jaha improvement chahiye, waha bol sakte ho, 'One area to consider improving is...' Aur end mein, ek suggestion do. Jaise, 'Going forward, it might help to...' Remember, 'this is wrong' jaise absolute negative language avoid karni hai. Isse tumhara feedback constructive rehta hai. Toh ab jab bhi feedback do, positive shuru karo, specific point batao, aur ek helpful suggestion do. Ab samajh aaya? Comment mein batao, aapko ye framework pata tha? Aur save kar lo ye reel for your next feedback session!

slides.body: Giving constructive feedback professionally is crucial for team growth and development. A helpful framework starts with a positive observation, then addresses a specific area for improvement, and concludes with a forward-looking suggestion. Use phrases like 'One thing that worked really well was...', 'One area to consider improving is...', and 'Going forward, it might help to...'. Remember to avoid absolute negative language like 'this is wrong' to keep the conversation supportive and productive. This approach fosters development without demotivating the recipient.
